title: `sum` of integers: widened below 32 bits, wraps at 32 and 64; 0 for no values
description: `sum` of `Int8`, `Int16`, `UInt8` and `UInt16` returns `Int64`; `Int32` and `Int64` keep their type and wrap, ungrouped and grouped (`Int32` 2³¹-1 + 1 is -2³¹).
The sum of no values, or of NULLs only, is 0, also per group: Substrait's `sum0`. `product` of no values is 1.
reference: `sum` of integers returns the input type, with `overflow: ERROR` (an inferred precondition checked on the data, #316, #437), and NULL for no values (`functions_arithmetic.yaml`: "The sum of zero elements yields null").

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
